summary: Pole platform built 1930, replaced by a 1934 pole tower; abandoned in the 1950s; footings still on site at a 2017 visit.

facts.design: 35-foot pole platform with log cabin (1930); 1934 pole tower with cab (size disputed)
facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1950s; a 2017 visit found concrete footings and lookout parts lying about.

access.note: Old jeep trail recently gated; a 2017 visit report says reaching the site now takes a two-mile hike. No closure order found.

visit.trail_note: About two miles on foot along the gated former jeep trail, per the 2017 visit report.

events.note: Pole tower replaced the 1930 platform; sources disagree on height and cab size
Panoramic photographs taken from the roof on September 29
Growden CCC camp crews began construction of the Skalawag Ridge road to the tower in November 1934 (newspaper dated November 23, 1934)
Second pole platform two miles northwest apparently still there
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register as US 1465, WA 365
Visit report: site overgrown; concrete footings and lookout parts remain; old jeep trail gated

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Former Fire Lookout Sites register and firelookout.com give a 60-foot pole tower with a 7x7 cab; WillhiteWeb gives 40 feet with a 12x12 cab. The story reports both and does not choose.
Early maps (1928-1943) use Skalawag and later maps (from 1952) use Scalawag; the brief and the story use Skalawag Ridge.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on the 1934 tower: 60 ft with a 7x7 cab (FFLOS, firelookout.com) versus 40 ft with a 12x12 cab (WillhiteWeb); the story reports both. No staffing history or notable fires found in two web searches and several reads, so the story leaves them out. The newest source is a 2017 visit report, so current condition is not known. The gated jeep trail is not described as closed. The Wikimedia Commons Forest Service azimuth diagram was seen in search results only and is not a photo find here.
